published_prior_art.cite: ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 supplies the fixed-design efficiency ingredients; MareisDrton2026 already studies cost-aware efficiency-optimal partial measurement in a distinct linear front-door model.
ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 supplies the fixed-system bound; the proposed ordering is its profiled-value comparison specialized to a finite design list.

WangWangMiao2023 and GuptaLiptonChilders2024 establish pilot/online efficiency-bound allocation ideas; the finite argmin regret inequality is routine but applies them to design-specific bridge systems.
ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 gives fixed-system cross-fitted bridge inference, while independent pilot splitting makes the finite-design extension plausible but not a new statistical frontier by itself.

CarneiroLeeWilhelm2020 proves prediction-equivalence only for randomized regression adjustment; LalImbensHull2026 concerns a distinct linear noisy-surrogate model; neither gives a bridge-model prediction-to-efficiency approximation ratio.

novelty_flags.label: related_work; lem:designwise-gradient; seed:predictive-impossibility
novelty_flags.one_line: The core repeatedly attributes the fixed-system efficiency bound to ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 Theorem 4, but that theorem is a consistency result; the efficiency lower bound is Theorem 7, using the Theorem 5 variance.

soundness_flags.label: sampling_model; definition of \widehat\tau_B; thm:postselection-wald
soundness_flags.one_line: The main study is assigned the oracle share \alpha^*_{\widehat d_m}(P), but no pilot-based feasible estimator \widehat\alpha_m is defined, so the advertised implemented estimator and Wald theorem use the unknown law P.

soundness_flags.label: thm:postselection-wald
soundness_flags.one_line: The theorem invokes uniform bridge product-rate and variance-consistency hypotheses, but neither condition is an assumption in the core; they must be stated precisely, including the rates and uniformity domain.

soundness_flags.label: thm:pairwise-ordering
soundness_flags.one_line: After defining \Delta_P(d,d') as the difference of profiled values, dominance iff \Delta_P(d,d')\le0 is only a definition/algebra unfold and should be a corollary or definition, not a substantive theorem target.

accepted_scope_caveats.label: lem:designwise-gradient through thm:pilot-oracle-regret
accepted_scope_caveats.caveat: These supporting results are conditional on every candidate design satisfying the fixed-system bridge, uniqueness, bijectivity, and finite-variance regularity inherited from the anchor model.
accepted_scope_caveats.bound_claim: The profile, ordering, and pilot-regret claims are asserted only on the nonempty regular-law class \mathfrak P_{\mathcal D}; the novelty claim remains the predictive-selection question on an open regular region.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 5, Theorem 4 and Theorems 5 and 7 (journal HTML lines 437-479)
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: Theorem 4 establishes consistency of OTC, SEL, and DR estimators; Theorem 5 gives the asymptotic variance and Theorem 7 identifies that variance as the local semiparametric efficiency lower bound under unique bridges and bijective T.

source_verification_receipts.locator: Section 3, especially pp. 7-8 / equations (3.2)-(3.3) and prediction-equivalence discussion
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper considers completely randomized treatment and rewrites its cost-constrained covariate/sample-size MSE objective as an outcome-prediction problem.

The paper studies efficiency gains from surrogate observations when the primary outcome is limited, under unconfounded treatment assignment and missingness, rather than selecting sequential bridge roles.
The paper formulates many noisy observed proxies of latent surrogates and analyzes regularized regression versus naive screening in a linear latent-variable surrogate model.

source_verification_receipts.version: Proceedings of the Fifth Conference on Causal Learning and Reasoning, PMLR 323, 2026, pp. 1068-1096
source_verification_receipts.verified_claim: The paper derives a cost-aware closed-form optimal partial-measurement policy and estimator for multivariate additive-noise linear front-door models, distinct from the proposed persistent-confounding bridge model.

strengthening_paths.suggestion: Define a pilot-feasible \widehat\alpha_m from \widehat V_{E,d},\widehat V_{O,d}, use it in the main-study sample counts, and prove the allocation plug-in error is negligible for the selected-design Wald pivot.
Replace every reference to ImbensKallusMaoWang2025 Theorem 4 as an efficiency result with Theorems 5 and 7, and anchor the exact variance formula to the cited theorem and sample-ratio convention.

Promote the predictive kernel by committing a small finite-support or Gaussian two-design witness family with explicit predictor tie-breaking, fixed prediction-risk ordering, bounded bridge moments, and an operator singular-value path driving \rho_{pred} to infinity.

Demote pairwise ordering to a definition/corollary and make the paper’s nontrivial field result the constructed open-region separation or a derived finite approximation constant under a primitive operator-comparability condition.

recommended_next_step: Revise the implementable allocation and explicit uniform bridge-rate assumptions, correct the anchor citation, and retain the open predictive-impossibility construction as the sole field-level novelty kernel.
